The venerable Upāli was questioned about the Vinaya by the venerable Mahākassapa. Devadatta asks the king for a blanket. They asked me for horses. Father, he asks you for wealth. The brahmin asks the nāga for the jewel. The nāga was asked for the jewel by the brahmin; the Blessed One was entreated by Brahmā for a Dhamma teaching. The ascetic begs for food from the family. He leads the goat to the village. The goat was led to the village. The freed Campeyyaka Nāga said this to the king.

Ettha rājānanti mukhyato kammaṃ vuttaṃ. Etanti guṇato. Tathā rājānanti akathitakammaṃ vuttaṃ. Etanti kathitakammaṃ. Esa nayo aññatrāpi upaparikkhitvā yathārahaṃ yojetabbo. Evameva “brūhi bhagavā”tiādīsu sampadānavisayattā dvikammakabhāvo na labbhati. Bhikkhu mahārājānaṃ dhammaṃ bhaṇati. Yaṃ maṃ bhaṇasi sārathi. Yaṃ maṃ vadati. Bhagavantaṃ etadavoca. Pitā puttaṃ bhāsati. Yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ anusāsasi. Sakyā kho pana ambaṭṭha rājānaṃ okkākaṃ pitāmahaṃ dahanti. Bhagavā bhikkhū taṃ taṃ hitapaṭipattiṃ nāthati. Gāvo vajaṃ rundhati gopālako. Dhutto dhuttajanaṃ dhanaṃ jināti. Ettha ca “kamanuttaraṃ ratnavaraṃ jināmā”ti puṇṇakajātakapāḷi nidassanaṃ. Tatthāyamattho “mayaṃ janindā kataraṃ rājānaṃ anuttaraṃ ratnavaraṃ jināmā”ti. Iṭṭhakāyo pākāraṃ cinoti vaḍḍhakī. Aññānipi yojetabbāni.

Here, 'rājānaṃ' is said to be the primary object, and 'etaṃ' the secondary. Similarly, 'rājānaṃ' is said to be the unstated object, and 'etaṃ' the stated object. This principle should be examined elsewhere and applied as is fitting. Likewise, in phrases like 'brūhi bhagavā' (Speak, O Blessed One), the state of having two objects is not obtained because it is in the sphere of the dative. A bhikkhu recites the Dhamma to the great king. 'What you say to me, charioteer.' 'What he says to me.' 'He said this to the Blessed One.' A father speaks to his son. 'What you instruct me.' The Sakyans, O Ambaṭṭha, hold King Okkāka to be their ancestor. The Blessed One guides the bhikkhus in this and that beneficial practice. A cowherd confines the cattle in a pen. A gambler wins wealth from another gambler. And here, the Pāli from the Puṇṇaka Jātaka, 'kamanuttaraṃ ratnavaraṃ jināmā,' is an example. The meaning there is: 'From which king, O lord of men, shall we win the supreme and excellent jewel?' A builder builds a wall with bricks. Other examples should also be construed.

Ettha [M 0.0390] keci puccheyyuṃ “gandhakuṭiṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karoti, buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretū’ti payogesu kiṃ dvikammakabhāvo labbhatī”ti? Ettha vuccate – “gandhakuṭiṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karotī”ti ettha na labbhati guṇaguṇīnaṃ vasena gahitattā. “Buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti etthāpi na labbhati “saraṇaṃ iti gacchāmī”ti itisaddalopavasena vuttattā. Tathā hi buddhanti upayogavacanaṃ. Saraṇanti paccattavacanaṃ. “Buddhaṃ mama saraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ, aghassa tātā hitassa ca vidhātā”ti iminā adhippāyena “bhajāmi sevāmi bujjhāmī”ti attho. “Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretū”ti ettha pana dvikammakabhāvo labbhatīti vattabbo “maṃ ito paṭṭhāya upāsakaṃ dhāretū”ti atthasambhavato “sakyā kho pana ambaṭṭha rājānaṃ okkākaṃ pitāmahaṃ dahantī”ti dahadhātuppayogena samānattā ca, adhippāyatthato pana “maṃ ‘upāsako me aya’nti dhāretū”ti attho sambhavatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ akāritāni dvikammikadhāturūpāni vibhāvitāni.

Here some might ask: 'In the usages “gandhakuṭiṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karoti” (he circumambulates the perfumed chamber), “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi” (I go for refuge to the Buddha), and “upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretū” (may the venerable Gotama regard me as a lay follower), is the state of having two objects obtained?' Here it is said: In 'gandhakuṭiṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karoti,' it is not obtained, because it is taken in the sense of a quality and the qualified. In 'buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi,' it is also not obtained, because it is stated with the elision of the word 'iti,' as in 'saraṇaṃ iti gacchāmi' (I go, thinking 'refuge'). For here, 'buddhaṃ' is a word of connection, and 'saraṇaṃ' is a word in the nominative. With the intention that 'The Buddha is my refuge, my ultimate resort, the remover of suffering and the provider of welfare,' the meaning is 'I resort to, I serve, I understand.' However, in 'upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretū,' it should be said that the state of having two objects is obtained, because the meaning 'May he regard me as a lay follower from now on' is possible, and because it is similar to the usage of the root 'dah' in 'sakyā kho pana ambaṭṭha rājānaṃ okkākaṃ pitāmahaṃ dahanti' (The Sakyans, O Ambaṭṭha, hold King Okkāka to be their ancestor). From the standpoint of intended meaning, however, it should be seen that the meaning 'May he regard me as, “This is my lay follower”' is possible. Thus, non-causative ditransitive verb forms have been explained.

Iccevamamhehi ādito paṭṭhāya bhagavato sāsanatthaṃ yathāsatti yathābalaṃ dhātuyo ca taṃrūpāni ca tadanurūpehi nānāpadehi nānāatthehi nānānayehi ca yojetvā vibhāvitāni, evaṃ vibhāventehipi amhehi tāsaṃ sarūpaparicchedo atthaparicchedo vā na sakkā sabbaso vattuṃ. Tadubhayañhi ko sabbaso vattuṃ sakkhissati aññatra āgamādhigamasampannehi pabhinnapaṭisambhidehi mahākhīṇāsavehi.

Thus, by us, from the very beginning, for the sake of the Blessed One’s teaching, according to our ability and strength, the roots and their forms have been explained by combining them with various corresponding terms, various meanings, and various methods. Yet, even as we thus explain them, we cannot fully define their exact forms or meanings. For who could fully explain both, other than those accomplished in both scripture and realization, who have attained the analytical knowledges, the great ones whose taints are destroyed?

Atthātisayayuttāpi, dhātū honti yato tato. Payogatonugantabbā, anekatthā hi dhātavo.

Though roots are endowed with an abundance of meanings, they are from various sources. They must be understood through their usage, for indeed, roots have many meanings.

Yenekatthadharā [M 0.0391] caranti vividhā nāthassa pāṭhe vare,

Tenekatthadharāva honti sahitā nānūpasaggehive;

Dhātūnaṃ pana tesamatthaparamaṃ khīṇāsave paṇḍite,

Vajjetvā paṭisambhidāmatiyute ko sabbaso bhaṇatīti.

The diverse roots that bear a single meaning function within the Lord's excellent teaching; likewise, they retain a single meaning even when joined with various prefixes. But as for the ultimate meaning of those roots, who can declare it in its entirety, except for the wise ones whose taints are destroyed, endowed with the wisdom of the analytical knowledges?

Iti navaṅge sāṭṭhakathe piṭakattaye byappathagatīsu viññūnaṃ

Thus, for the wise, in the paths of expression within the nine-limbed Teaching with its commentaries, and in the three Piṭakas,

Kosallatthāya kate saddanītippakaraṇe

in the treatise Saddanīti, made for the purpose of skill,

Sabbagaṇavinicchayo nāma ekūnavīsatimo paricchedo

the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Determination of All Verb Groups'.

Saha rūpavibhāvanāya dhātuvibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of roots, together with the explanation of forms, is completed.

Dhātumālā niṭṭhitā.

The Garland of Roots is completed.
